tasks.title: Simple CASE
tasks.statement: Output the order id and a status label: `'new'` — `'open'`, `'paid'` — `'settled'`, `'shipped'` — `'dispatched'`, `'cancelled'` — `'voided'`. Columns id, status_label; ordered by id.
tasks.hint: CASE expression WHEN value THEN result … END

tasks.title: Conditions in CASE
tasks.statement: Output title, price and the price class tier: under 1000 — `'cheap'`, from 1000 to 9999 — `'average'`, from 10000 — `'expensive'`. Ordered by id.
tasks.hint: CASE WHEN condition THEN … ELSE … END; branches are checked top to bottom.

tasks.title: Without ELSE
tasks.statement: Output name and a label: 'VIP' for VIP customers, NULL for the rest (no ELSE). Ordered by id.
tasks.hint: Without ELSE, non-matching rows get NULL.

tasks.title: Default city
tasks.statement: Output name and the city; if there is no city — `'unknown'` (via CASE WHEN city IS NULL …). Columns name, city_label; ordered by id.

tasks.title: VIP flag
tasks.statement: Output name and vip_text: `'yes'` if vip = 1, otherwise `'no'`. Ordered by id.

tasks.title: Stock level
tasks.statement: Output title and the stock status stock_status: 0 — `'out of stock'`, less than 20 — `'low'`, otherwise `'enough'`. Ordered by id.

tasks.title: Order size
tasks.statement: Output id and the order size size: total ≥ 40000 — `'large'`, ≥ 5000 — `'medium'`, otherwise `'small'`. Ordered by id.

tasks.title: Custom sort order
tasks.statement: Output the id and status of orders in the required status order: new, paid, shipped, cancelled; within a status — by id. ORDER BY with CASE.
tasks.hint: CASE turns a status into a number for sorting.

tasks.title: VIPs first
tasks.statement: Output name and vip: VIP customers (vip = 1) first, then the rest; within groups — by name. ORDER BY CASE.

tasks.title: IIF
tasks.statement: IIF(condition, yes, no) is a short form of CASE. Output title and `IIF(stock = 0, 'no', 'yes')` as available; ordered by id.

tasks.title: Nested CASE
tasks.statement: Output title and group_label: for the category `'Tech'` — `'pricey'` if price ≥ 40000, otherwise `'regular'`; for the other categories — `'not tech'`. Ordered by id.

tasks.title: Comparing columns
tasks.statement: Output title and note: `'stock above price'` if stock > price, otherwise `'normal'`. Ordered by id.

tasks.title: Counting by class
tasks.statement: In a single row, output the number of products in the price classes: cheap (< 1000), mid (1000–9999), pricey (≥ 10000) using SUM(CASE WHEN … THEN 1 ELSE 0 END).

tasks.title: Revenue by status
tasks.statement: In a single row, output the order totals: paid_sum — for status 'paid', new_sum — for 'new' (SUM(CASE WHEN … THEN total ELSE 0 END)).

tasks.title: Cancellation share
tasks.statement: Output the share of cancelled orders in percent, rounded to a whole number: ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*)) as cancel_pct.

tasks.title: Division by zero guard
tasks.statement: Output title and price / stock as ratio; if stock = 0 — NULL (use CASE). Ordered by id.

tasks.title: Order discount
tasks.statement: Output the order id, total and total_with_discount: for a total over 40000 — with a 10% discount (total * 90 / 100), otherwise no discount. Ordered by id.

tasks.title: Delivery cost
tasks.statement: Output name and delivery: 0 for Moscow (`'Moscow'`), 500 if the city is unknown (NULL), otherwise 300. Ordered by id.

tasks.title: Mail provider
tasks.statement: Output name and provider: 'gmail' if the email ends with @gmail.com, 'mail' for @mail.ru, 'yandex' for @yandex.ru, 'other' for the rest, and 'no email' for NULL. Ordered by id.

tasks.title: The CASE and NULL trap
tasks.statement: CASE city WHEN NULL … never fires (NULL = NULL is unknown). Output the number of customers that got the label `'empty'` from the expression `CASE city WHEN NULL THEN 'empty' ELSE 'yes' END` (it will be 0) as n.
tasks.hint: For NULL you need CASE WHEN city IS NULL.

tasks.title: CASE instead of COALESCE
tasks.statement: Output name and contact: the email if there is one, otherwise the city, otherwise `'no data'` — using CASE. Ordered by id.

tasks.title: HR: seniority
tasks.statement: HR database. Output name and seniority: hired before 2020 — `'veteran'`, 2020–2022 — `'experienced'`, later — `'newcomer'`. Use hired < '2020-01-01' and the like. Ordered by id.

tasks.title: HR: bonus by level
tasks.statement: HR database. Output name and bonus: lead — 20% of salary, senior — 15%, middle — 10%, junior — 5% (salary * percent / 100). Ordered by id.

tasks.title: HR: department or a note
tasks.statement: HR database. Output name and dept: the department name from the departments table, and if there is no department — `'no department'`. LEFT JOIN and CASE. Ordered by id.

tasks.title: HR: salary bands
tasks.statement: HR database. Output name and band: under 100000 — 'A', 100000–199999 — 'B', from 200000 — 'C'. Ordered by id.

tasks.title: HR: how many in each band
tasks.statement: HR database. In a single row: a_n, b_n, c_n — the number of employees in bands A, B, C from the previous exercise.

tasks.title: School: grade in words
tasks.statement: School database. For the 2024 records, output student_id, course_id and text: 5 — `'excellent'`, 4 — `'good'`, 3 — `'satisfactory'`, NULL — `'no rating'`. Ordered by student_id, course_id.

tasks.title: School: pass or fail
tasks.statement: School database. Output student_id, course_id and passed: 1 — grade 3 or higher, 0 — lower, NULL — no grade. For 2024; ordered by student_id, course_id.

tasks.title: School: grade distribution
tasks.statement: School database. In a single row: fives, fours, threes, none — the number of fives, fours, threes and empty grades for 2024.

tasks.title: School: level
tasks.statement: School database. Output name and level: classes `9A`/`9B` — `'middle school'`, classes 10–11 — `'high school'`. Ordered by id.

tasks.title: Movies: rating
tasks.statement: Movies database. Output title and verdict: rating ≥ 8.5 — `'masterpiece'`, ≥ 7.5 — `'good'`, otherwise `'average'`, NULL — `'no rating'`. Ordered by id.

tasks.title: Movies: era
tasks.statement: Movies database. Output title and era: year before 2005 — `'classic'`, 2005–2015 — `'recent'`, after 2015 — `'new'`. Ordered by id.

tasks.title: Movies: budget size
tasks.statement: Movies database. Output title and scale: budget ≥ 100 — `'blockbuster'`, otherwise `'modest'`, NULL — `'unknown'`. Ordered by id.

tasks.title: Movies: count by era
tasks.statement: Movies database. In a single row: classic_n (year < 2005), recent_n (2005–2015), new_n (> 2015) — the number of movies.
